clue.text: Men in further education giving warning on course

indicators.note: in says the men sit inside the abbreviation for further education

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the crossword's usual word for ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Men at a college shouting a warning across a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on course' means a golf course: the golfer's shout warning that a ball is heading your way.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers shout this word to alert people in the path of a struck ball.

clue.text: Outstanding Liverpudlian singer madly into swing

parts.note: O/S is the accounting abbreviation for outstanding, still owed
Cilla Black was a singer and TV presenter from Liverpool

indicators.note: madly says the letters of into are jumbled wildly

explanation.surface: A brilliant Liverpool singer throws herself frantically into swing music.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a 1960s pop star from Liverpool, later a popular British TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: An oscillation is a regular swinging movement back and forth.

clue.text: English mostly snigger about that French behavioural code

indicators.note: about says the shortened snigger goes round the French word
mostly says the snigger word loses its final letter

parts.note: to titter is to snigger
que is French for that

explanation.surface: An Englishman sniggers at French rules of polite behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TITTER to TITTE, which goes about QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the customary code of polite conduct in society.

clue.text: Fellow pupil beginning to serve chilled infusion outside hotel

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here taken from serve
outside says the chilled word wraps around the hotel letter

parts.note: chilled means cool
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
mate is a South American herbal infusion drunk like tea

explanation.surface: A recipe: start serving a cold herbal drink outside a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmate is a classmate or fellow pupil at the same school.

clue.text: Download Horace's first letter, thus written about like his odes

indicators.note: written about says the thus word is set down around the other letters

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to flag a quoted error
an app is a program you download

indicators.note: first letter picks the opening letter of Horace's

explanation.surface: Downloading Horace and reading about his ode style.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace wrote some of his Odes in the Sapphic stanza, the metre named after the Greek poet Sappho.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sapphic metre, from Sappho, is a stanza form Horace used in his Latin poems.

clue.text: Rebel leader from this place fighting duke on the Wash

parts.note: here means this place
war is fighting
a ship's wash is its wake, the trail of water behind it

explanation.surface: A rebel chief from these parts battles a duke beside the Wash.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large bay on England's east coast by the Fens, where Hereward held out against William the Conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward the Wake led English resistance to the Normans from the Isle of Ely around 1070.

clue.text: Former ace, a man with energy

parts.note: an ace counts as one
Tim is a man's name
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An ex-champion, an energetic man.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means previous or erstwhile, as in a one-time champion.

clue.text: Old Mexican Indian, a variable investigator

parts.note: z is a letter used for a variable in algebra
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: An ancient Mexican who turns out to be an unpredictable sleuth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the native people ruling central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Assistant replacing one in flight — one living abroad

indicators.note: replacing says the assistant takes the place of one in the flight word

parts.note: flight as in fleeing: an exit
I is the Roman numeral one
PA, personal assistant

explanation.surface: An assistant standing in for a colleague on a flight, someone who lives overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat, short for expatriate, lives outside their native country.

clue.text: First of several kittens edgy about cheerful little dog

indicators.note: about says those opening letters go around the word for cheerful
First of takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: chipper means cheerful, lively

explanation.surface: Several nervous kittens set about by a cheerful little dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' serves all three words, not just 'several'; 'about' then wraps those three letters around the cheerful word.
explanation.definitionFit: A schipperke is a small black Belgian breed, once a barge watchdog.

clue.text: Conclusion sometimes drawn by an organist

definitions.meaning: an organ ... is a knob pulled out to bring a set of pipes into play

explanation.surface: A recital ends with a final flourish from the organist.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is a stop; an organ's register knobs are also called stops, and they are drawn out.

clue.text: Swamp primarily surrounding Irish lake

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of surrounding

parts.note: lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: Bogland lying all around a lake in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a muddy marsh or bog.

clue.text: Wooden panelling in old wagons by country dwelling

parts.note: wain is an old word for a farm wagon, so wagons are wains
a cot is a small cottage in the countryside

explanation.surface: Old farm carts parked beside a cottage with panelled rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden lining on the lower part of a room's walls.

clue.text: Ubiquitous old politician with grudge about Islington area

indicators.note: about says the politician goes around the Islington code

parts.note: MP, member of parliament
N1 is the London postcode district for Islington, read here as NI
to resent something is to grudge it

explanation.surface: A former MP who resents a part of north London and is seen everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a district of north London with the postcode N1; the figure 1 stands as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipresent means present everywhere at once, the same as ubiquitous.

clue.text: Reportedly something that beats a mature male deer

indicators.note: Reportedly says the word for something that beats is to be heard, not read

parts.note: the heart beats in the chest

explanation.surface: Something with a beating heart: a full-grown stag.
explanation.definitionFit: A hart is an adult male red deer, especially one over five years old.

clue.text: Agree to exchange letters

definitions.meaning: things ... when they match or agree
to write letters to each other

explanation.surface: Two people decide to become pen pals.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both matching up and keeping up a written exchange with someone.

clue.text: Coming before what a hawk may be doing

definitions.text: what a hawk may be doing
definitions.meaning: ... also means hunting prey, which is what a hawk does

explanation.surface: A hawk swooping in ahead of its target.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling carries two senses: preceding in time, and acting as a predator.

clue.text: Fantastic eastern wit, a discriminating drinker

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly imaginative, telling us to rearrange the letters of eastern wit

explanation.surface: A witty oriental sage who is also fussy about what he drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine taster samples and judges wines, so is choosy about drink.

clue.text: Confusing names initially is a pathological condition

indicators.note: confusing means mixing up, so the letters of names are scrambled
initially takes the first letter of each of is and a

explanation.surface: Mixing up names at the outset is a symptom of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia, memory loss, is a medical disorder.

clue.text: Pay back half of rent? Absolutely

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of rent

parts.note: quite can mean absolutely, as in quite right

explanation.surface: A tenant pays back half the rent and is totally sure about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to repay or return a favour or injury.

clue.text: Catch a glimpse of some state's pyramids

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tourist glimpses the pyramids of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of something, often at a distance.

clue.text: Break in regularly after pinching item of jewellery

indicators.note: pinching says those alternate letters grip the jewellery word between them
regularly takes every other letter of after, the second and fourth

parts.note: a ring is an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: A thief breaks in again and again to steal a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a word placing IN, but 'regularly' works on it as fodder, and 'pinching' has its picked letters grip the jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule or law is to break it.

clue.text: Clubs criminals were sometimes clapped in?

explanation.surface: Clubs that prisoners were once put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are both golf clubs and the chains clapped on prisoners.

clue.text: Crook fleeces exec at first, taking half of capital

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of each of fleeces and exec
half of keeps the first three letters of the capital

parts.note: London is the capital of England

explanation.surface: A con man swindles an executive and makes off with half the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is a city, London.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is a criminal, someone guilty of a serious crime.

clue.text: Note that makes us tremble!

definitions.meaning: a musical note, an eighth note
to tremble, especially of a voice

explanation.surface: A musical note so frightening it makes the listeners shake.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical note shares its name with a shaky, trembling sound.

clue.text: Sole Liberal in west end of Oklahoma City

indicators.note: on a map west is the left, so the west end of Oklahoma is its first letter
in places the Liberal letter inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY, New York, is the crossword's usual city

explanation.surface: The lone Liberal living in the western part of Oklahoma City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'west end' reads as a district of the city but picks the leftmost letter, O, of Oklahoma.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole and only both mean single, the one and no other.

clue.text: Repaired rail is best steadying device

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so the letters of rail is best are reassembled

explanation.surface: A fixed handrail is the best way to keep steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A stabiliser keeps a ship, aircraft or bicycle steady.

clue.text: Africans visit Kent area, taking in Tyneside lass

indicators.note: taking in says the visit word wraps around the Tyneside lass

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
NE, north-east England, where Tyneside lies
gal is an informal word for a girl or lass
SE, south-east England, where Kent lies

explanation.surface: African tourists visiting Kent with a Geordie girl in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England and Kent is a county in the south-east, hence NE and SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Senegalese are the people of Senegal, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Follower of 1980s subculture became stylish in the end

parts.note: got can mean became, as in got angry

indicators.note: in the end takes the last letter of stylish

explanation.surface: Someone who finally turned fashionable in the eighties.
explanation.definitionFit: Goths, with black clothes and dark makeup, grew out of the 1980s post-punk music scene.
